summary: Delayed TTFB and 504s for long-sequence completions caused by ALB keepalive churn + proxy buffering
description:
Issue summary:
Customers running long-generation requests (2000+ token completions) intermittently see very large time-to-first-byte (TTFB) or final 504s despite backend logs indicating model started generating. Impact: several enterprise customers on Dedicated experienced increased error rates and perceived performance regressions since 2026-03-07.

Impact:
- LexaDocs reported ~8% error rate on long completions; user-facing slow requests and failed job retries.
- Symptom pattern: request accepted, no bytes for 8–30s, then ALB or gateway returns 504 or connection reset. In other cases first bytes arrive but final completion truncated.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (us-east-1) behind ALB -> nginx sidecar -> serving runtime.
- Large tracing headers and cookie payloads (custom CSRF + jwt rotation) present for affected customers.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Send a streaming generate with prompt resulting in >2000 token completion and long KV-cache warmup on cold path.
2) Include a 12–18KB X-Trace header and persistent cookie set.
3) Observe TTFB spike 10–25s on ~1/20 attempts; ALB logs frequently show Target: Connection closed by client or idle timeout.

Attachments / artifacts:
- Relevant ALB access logs: s3://redwood-logs/alb/2026/03/07/lexadocs.log.gz
- Nginx sidecar error logs (snippets in comments)
- Serving-runtime traces: trace ids 20260309-lexa-01..05

Initial hypothesis:
- ALB connection reuse/keepalive churn + large headers cause HPACK fragmentation and reorder; nginx proxy buffering combined with no bytes from model early (KV cold path) results in ALB treating the connection idle and closing it (ALB idle timeout ~15s).
- Proxy buffering rules can delay flushing of headers/body until buffer thresholds met, making TTFB appear larger.

Urgency and customer impact:
High — enterprise customers seeing production errors. Workaround requested while we investigate permanent fixes.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-09 10:12 - Support: Got initial report from LexaDocs -> escalated to SRE; provided request IDs and sample timestamps.
2026-03-09 11:05 - SRE: Reproduced locally with synthetic traffic including large X-Trace header; saw TTFB spike when nginx proxy buffering not flushing until buffer full.

2026-03-09 13:20 - SRE: ALB access logs show Target: idle_timeout and Target: connection_reset entries aligned with delayed TTFB. Many of the affected requests used connection reuse with keepalive count > 5.

2026-03-10 09:40 - Eng: Correlated spikes with KV-cache cold paths where model backend does not emit bytes for first 6–12s. If no early partial bytes, nginx keeps response in buffer until buffer threshold or flush, which ALB treats as idle.
2026-03-11 15:02 - Eng: Tested disabling proxy_buffering in nginx sidecar for a dedicated subset; TTFB issues reduced in canary; however, we observed higher memory usage under heavy concurrency.

2026-03-12 08:50 - SRE: Identified that long headers (~16KB) push ALB HTTP/1.1 framing to exhibit head-of-line effects when connection reused; confirmed HPACK / h2 frame fragmentation increases latency on some flows.
2026-03-12 14:10 - Product: Notified affected customers of investigation and temporary mitigation.
comments: 2026-03-09 10:30 - Maya Chen (Support): Thank you for the report, Ethan. Can you confirm whether any retries are originating from client SDK? Also asking LexaDocs for sample request IDs.

2026-03-09 11:10 - Ethan Park (Support): Provided 5 request IDs to SRE: req-20260309-87a, req-20260309-92b, req-20260309-10c, req-20260309-14d, req-20260309-22e. Logs uploaded to s3 and shared in #support-lexadocs thread.

2026-03-09 11:20 - Liam O'Neill (SRE): Reproduced with a stress test. When nginx proxy_buffering is enabled and backend holds bytes >8s, ALB sometimes times out at 15s. Creating INT ticket for sidecar config options (INT-412).

2026-03-10 09:50 - Priya Patel (Customer Success): LexaDocs confirmed seeing improvements when we route a subset of traffic to dedicated machines with modified sidecar config; asking for a short-term config change for the customer's pool.

2026-03-11 16:30 - Liam O'Neill (SRE): Deployed canary with proxy_buffering disabled + more aggressive keepalive_timeout on 3 hosts. Early results: TTFB regressions dropped from 8% -> 0.9% for LexaDocs traffic in canary window.
2026-03-12 09:05 - Security (A. Ruiz): Large tracing headers and cookies noted; advise we also review header size policies and ensure customers cannot push >32KB headers in future. Added to backlog.
2026-03-12 14:30 - Maya Chen (Support): Notified LexaDocs of temporary mitigation and asked for monitoring confirmation for 24 hours.
workaround: Canary rollout: disable proxy_buffering on nginx sidecar for LexaDocs' dedicated pool and increase ALB target group deregistration/idle thresholds where safe. This reduces TTFB spikes but increases memory pressure on sidecars under concurrency.
root_cause: Interaction between ALB idle timeout + HTTP framing with large headers + nginx proxy_buffering combined with backend delayed-first-byte (KV-cache cold path). ALB considered connection idle and closed it before sidecar flushed buffered response chunks.
resolution: In progress — short-term mitigation applied (disable proxy_buffering for affected dedicated pool and increased sidecar memory). Medium-term plan: update default sidecar config to flush headers earlier for streaming endpoints, tune ALB target idle settings for Dedicated, and introduce header-size and HPACK fragmentation detection alerts. Engineering change request created.
resolution_fix: Planned changes: (1) Add early-flush on response headers for streaming paths in sidecar (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar/pull/557), (2) add ALB connection-age/idle tuning guidance for Dedicated customers, (3) implement server-side keepalive churn metrics and alerting.
postmortem_followup_items: Roll out early-flush sidecar change to all Dedicated pools (owner: serving-runtime)
Add automated tests that simulate large headers + cold KV path to CI
Update Dedicated onboarding docs with recommended ALB keepalive/idle settings
Add alert for ALB Target Idle timeouts >1% over 5m
